title: PARTICIPANT INFORMATION SHEET

header.sponsor: AI Centre of Excellence in Healthcare at TANUH Foundation, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore 560012
header.studyTitle: Development of an AI enabled Breast Cancer Risk Prediction Tool for the Indian Population
header.iecApproval: Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC), TANUH Foundation, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore 560012

paragraphs.text: This study is part of a Ministry of Education funded project to develop Indian AI solutions for Healthcare. TANUH Foundation is a section 8 company hosted by Indian Institute of Science proud to lead this critical national initiative in breast cancer research, recognizing that early, data-driven detection is vital for improving health outcomes. We deeply appreciate your participation and thank you for being an essential part of this effort to advance breast cancer study for the benefit of women across India. Make AI in India and Make AI work for India.

sections.heading: What is the purpose of the study?

paragraphs.text: Development of an AI enabled Breast Cancer Risk Prediction Tool for the Indian Population

You have been chosen to contribute towards the study of AI enabled breast cancer screening tools because you have been referred to mammography or getting a routine mammography. We are developing an AI enabled breast cancer screening tool that enables identification of breast cancer risk by a few questionnaires.

sections.heading: Do I have to take part?

paragraphs.text: Your participation is completely voluntary. You may opt not to participate in the study and continue with your normal routine.

sections.heading: What Will Happen in the Study If you agree to participate, the following will occur?

paragraphs.text: Survey: You will be asked to fill out a one-time questionnaire (on a tablet/digital device) regarding your demographics, health history, lifestyle, and family history of cancer.
Risk Prediction: At the end of the survey, you will be provided with an immediate breast cancer risk prediction (identifying if you are at normal or higher risk).

Guidance: Based on the risk level, you will receive guidance. If you are found to be at higher risk, you may be referred for mammography. If you are at normal/low risk, you will be asked to continue regular checkup protocols.
Data Usage: The data collected from you and from the hospital will be used to train an Artificial Intelligence (AI) model to better predict breast cancer risk in Indian women.

sections.heading: What will happen to me if I take part?

paragraphs.text: The personalized risk prediction will help you to be more aware of possible breast cancer symptoms and your individual risk factors for future health monitoring.

sections.heading: What do I have to do?

paragraphs.text: You need to complete a one-time questionnaire about lifestyle, family history, and demographics health-related factors at https://bc-portal-dev.tanuh.ai/. It will also involve you following a video-based tutorial on self-breast examination and answering questions. At any point of time, the nurse staff will be able to guide you through the process and complete the questionnaire.

sections.heading: What are the possible risks of taking part?

paragraphs.text: There are no known major risks in taking part in this research study.
No/Minimal Risk: This study is considered "no/minimal risk".
Privacy: There is a rare risk regarding privacy, but this is mitigated because we do not collect personally identifiable information, and data is captured anonymously.
Voluntary: The questionnaire is completely voluntary; if you are not interested, you may pursue routine clinic care instead.
No Invasive Procedures: This is a digital and workflow innovation study; no experimental drugs or invasive therapies are involved in the research component.

sections.heading: What are the possible benefits of taking part?

paragraphs.text: Personal Benefit: There is likely no direct benefit for individual participants. However, you will receive a risk prediction that may help inform your screening strategy.
Societal Benefit: Your participation will contribute to scientific benefits, including enhanced early detection of breast cancer and better resource allocation for women across India.

sections.heading: Will my taking part in this study be kept confidential?

paragraphs.text: Yes. All information collected during this study will be kept strictly confidential. All personal data will be anonymized and stored securely in accordance with applicable data protection regulations. Only authorized research team members will have access to the data, and no personally identifiable information will be shared with third parties without your explicit consent. The study results will be presented in aggregate form only, ensuring individual participants cannot be identified.

About 20% of the total data, collected in an irreversible anonymised manner, will be part of the benchmarking and open data initiative of TANUH for evaluation of AI algorithms. The data collected will be used in future research, including the development of other foundation models.
Your participation is entirely voluntary. You can refuse to participate or stop the survey at any time without penalty or loss of benefits.

sections.heading: Are there any compensation and Medical Care for Research-Related Injury?

paragraphs.text: Compensation: You will not be paid for participating in this study. No compensation is offered as this is a minimal/no-risk study.
Injury: As this is a survey/AI-based screening study involving no invasive interventions, no medical treatment or compensation for injury is planned.
Costs: There is no cost to you for participating in this study.

sections.heading: What will happen to the results of the research study?

paragraphs.text: The results of this research study will be used to develop and validate an AI enabled Breast Cancer Risk Prediction tool. Findings may be published in peer-reviewed scientific journals, presented at academic conferences, and shared with healthcare institutions and policymakers to improve breast cancer screening practices in India. All published results will be in aggregate form with no individual identification.

sections.heading: Who is organising and funding the research?

paragraphs.text: This research is being organized and funded by the AI Centre of Excellence in Healthcare at TANUH Foundation, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore 560012.
This study has been reviewed by the Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC), TANUH Foundation, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore 560012.

informedConsent.title: INFORMED CONSENT FORM

paragraphs.text: Your participation in this study is voluntary. You may refuse to participate in this study or in any part of this study at any time. Likewise the investigator also retains the right to terminate your participation in the experiment at any time without giving a reason. The decision to withdraw or terminate your participation will not affect your relations with your institute/university/hospital or affect the care you receive. You are encouraged to ask questions about this study any time during the study.

sections.heading: Information collected as part of this study

paragraphs.text: Demographics, lifestyle, family history, menstrual and reproductive health information - necessary
Mammograms along with report (necessary)
ultrasound and/or biopsy report (optional)

Data Anonymization: All information gathered in this study will be collected, processed, and stored in an irreversibly anonymized manner to ensure your privacy. Collected information storage adheres to the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act standards.
The data collected will be used in future research, including the development of other foundation models.

Rights: You have the right to access and correct your personal data and to withdraw your consent for research processing at any time. The decision to withdraw will not affect the regular clinical care you receive.

Retention: Your irreversibly anonymized data and samples may be stored for as long as they are useful for lawful research and required safeguards are in place, in accordance with the DPDP Act and other legal or regulatory obligations.
If you wish to speak to someone independent of the study as well as withdrawal of the consent, you may contact the Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC)
